title: PRD: Granular lane contracts with operational backstops and launch checklist
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: define a PRD that formalizes lane-level behavioral contracts (fast / balanced / cost), explicit operational backstops, and a step-by-step launch checklist for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank hosted endpoints. This ticket scopes acceptance criteria, rollout slices, telemetry-based abort conditions, fallback mappings, and post-launch guardrails so teams can ship lane-aware pricing and SLAs without regressing quality or availability.
goals: Provide clear, testable lane contracts for latency and quality across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Ensure safe cutover with automated rollback triggers based on telemetry and quality evals
Ship packaging that enables customers to select lanes with predictable cost/latency trade-offs
Integrate canary rollouts, graded fallbacks, and on-call runbook entries for each lane
out_of_scope: Changes to pricing model (billing ownership remains pricing team)
Rewriting runtime kernel selection logic (engineering runtime performance optimization will be separate tickets)
New model architecture onboarding (model-specific tuning handled by model ops)
requirements: API: lane selector param on create/route (lane: fast|balanced|cost) preserved across retries
Behavioral contracts: per-lane SLAs and quality gates defined and stored in registry
Fallbacks: automated downgrade chain (fast -> balanced -> cost -> conformant fallbacks) with explicit cost/latency mapping
Telemetry: per-lane p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, error-rate, and eval-quality signals visible in Console
Evals: baseline prompt suite and embedding similarity checks for embeddings/rerank to run in preflight and post-deploy
Operational: runbook entries, SLO burn dashboards, and one-click rollback from Console
Docs: public API doc updates and migration notes for existing clients
success_metrics: Customer-facing SLA attainment: >=95% of customer requests observe lane contract for p99 latency over a 24h window
Quality preservation: downstream eval score regressions <= 2% vs baseline across batched eval set
Adoption: 15% of active customers try lane selector within first 8 weeks
Cost predictability: documented per-token unit-cost within +/-10% for each lane during steady state
acceptance_criteria: A1: API accepts a lane parameter and returns a lane identifier in response headers
A2: Per-lane p99 latency targets validated on staging with synthetic traffic: fast <= 250ms (gen token latency), balanced <= 450ms, cost <= 900ms
A3: Embeddings similarity: average cosine drift <= 0.01 on baseline probe set after lane changes
A4: Rerank NDCG@10 delta <= 0.015 vs control for balanced lane
A5: Canary flow: run 5% traffic for 24h with automatic quality checks; abort if error-rate increase >50% or eval regression >1.5%
A6: Console: lane telemetry widgets and SLO burn alert integrated into existing incident pages
A7: Runbooks: on-call playbook updated and validated in a tabletop exercise
A8: Docs: public specs and migration guide published and linked from Console
launch_checklist: Preflight: complete eval baseline (gen, embed, rerank) and commit artifact hashes to registry
Pre-merge: API contract reviewed by SDK/Docs and security review completed
Staging: run synthetic load across lanes to capture p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token estimates
Canary: 5% traffic slice for 24h with real traffic from internal customers; run eval checks every 4h
Operational hooks: enable SLO alerts, add burn dashboards to on-call rotation, and verify rollback button in Console works
Customer comms: prepare migration note, public changelog entry, and sample SDK snippet
Final gate: sign-off from Product, Eng, SRE, and Docs
rollout_plan: T0 - Staging validation (team internal): synthetic + eval suite pass
T1 - Canary (5%): open canary for 24h, automated quality checks running
T2 - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 72h windows if no abort triggers
T3 - Global enable: widen to 100% with monitoring at lane-level metrics
Post-launch: 2-week monitoring window and weekly cadence for quality regression reviews
telemetry_signals: Per-lane latency p50/p95/p99 (gen token and end-to-end request)
Error rates: 4xx vs 5xx split and increased timeouts
Throughput: tokens/sec per GPU pool and per-tenant
Eval_quality: periodic batch eval scores (generation BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies, embedding cosine drift, rerank NDCG)
Cost metrics: per-token charge estimates and effective CPU/GPU utilization
dependencies: ENG-21012: lane-parameter routing in API gateway
ENG-21890: per-lane telemetry tagging in runtime
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: lane selection increases fragmentation of caches leading to higher tail latency. Mitigation: implement cross-lane prefix caching whitelist and measure cache hit delta in staging.

Risk: customers misconfigure and hit cost lane inadvertently. Mitigation: default to balanced, show clear cost warnings in Console, and require explicit opt-in for cost lane in accounts > enterprise tier.
Risk: eval suites do not surface edge-case regressions. Mitigation: include production-sampled probes and a lightweight A/B quality harness during canary.
Risk: rollback button fails under load. Mitigation: pre-test rollback under synthetic peak load and provide manual operator runbook
decisions: D1: Use three lanes (fast|balanced|cost) to balance complexity and customer choice
D2: Canary slice size set to 5% for initial rollout to maximize signal while limiting blast radius
D3: Default lane for new customers is 'balanced' to avoid surprise cost exposure
D4: Embeddings drift threshold selected as 0.01 cosine based on historical model variance
open_questions: Q1: Should enterprise accounts be allowed to define custom lane profiles or only use presets? (Product decision required)
Q2: Do we expose lane in SDKs as enum or free-form string to allow future expansion? (SDK teams to decide)
Q3: What retention window for per-lane telemetry (30d default? 90d for enterprise?)
